findings.F1: Across all coins and windows w7–w18, closes above the prior 20-day closing high are followed by the largest unusual 5-day rises, and the rise grows with the height above that high. Closes 0 to 1 daily swings above it gain +3.14 % (121 cases, 61 days, t 1.94, strength 0.27, 52 % up). Closes more than 1 swing above it gain +10.03 % (71 cases, 44 days, t 1.66, strength 0.48, 58 % up). Both bands are positive in each half: w7–12 +2.76 % / +14.51 %, w13–18 +3.50 % / +4.58 %.
findings.F2: The rise after a close at or above the 20-day high holds in every trend profile. Rising: +6.15 % (74 cases, 32 days, t 2.41, strength 0.49). Falling: +4.01 % (19 cases, 8 days, t 3.29). Choppy: +24.24 % (22 cases, 16 days, t 1.36). A close above its prior 20-day range gives +5.57 % (193 cases, t 2.44).
findings.F3: Over the whole range, the 5-day unusual move rises with distance from the high (the strength rises by 0.063 per swing, day-clustered t 2.37, 2016 cases). The relation is positive in both halves (t 2.05 and 1.44) and in 9 of 12 coins. It is steepest in choppy markets: slope 0.22 per swing, Spearman 0.28, t 2.70, 189 cases. In rising markets it is 0.12 (t 2.21) and in falling ones 0.04 (t 0.87).
findings.F4: In choppy markets, closes more than 1.5 swings below the 20-day high fall by an unusual 4.49 % over 5 days (116 cases, 55 days, t −2.31, strength −0.35, 34 % up). Beyond that point the depth does not grade the fall. Across all trends the bands give −1.88 % (beyond −4 swings), −0.45 % (−4 to −3) and −1.49 % (−3 to −2). This flat response is why the supporting check failed.
findings.F5: The book's short side cannot pay. Its total move per case is +0.08 %, 0.4 times the 0.22 % cost, because the coins' normal drift works −0.80 % against the short. The long side above the high has the drift with it and an unusual move of +3 % to +10 %, more than ten times the cost.
findings.F6: The book's result rests on a few days. Its 10 best days sum to +62 % and its 10 worst to −44 %, while its total over all days is about 1/6 of the 10 best. Its windows run from −21 % (w10) to +24 % (w16), with no steady gain (Sharpe 0.03).
findings.F7: Weekday effects do not stand out given how many angles were examined. Wednesday and Saturday signals were followed by −3.2 % and −3.3 % (t −2.02 and −1.97, about 35 days each), but the two halves disagree in strength (Wednesday t −2.77 vs −0.94). This is not counted as a finding for an idea.

ideas.idea: A daily close above the coin's highest close of the prior 20 days is followed by a rise over the next 5 days, larger the more of the coin's 20-day daily swings it stands above that high.
ideas.consequence: A trader would buy closes that break above the 20-day high, sizing by how far above it they close in daily swings, in every market rather than only rising ones.
ideas.name: breakout above high rises

ideas.idea: In a choppy market, the higher a daily close sits against the coin's 20-day high, counted in its 20-day daily swings, the more the coin rises over the next 5 days. This runs from falls far below the high to rises above it.
ideas.consequence: A trader in a flat-trend coin would lean long as the close nears and breaks its 20-day high and lean short as it sinks below it, sized by the distance in swings.
ideas.name: choppy distance-from-high gradient
